blocks.content: Soil erosion is defined as the destruction and removal of the topsoil cover by natural agents such as running water and wind.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Soil erosion involves the detachment and transportation of the fertile topsoil layer by physical agents like running water and wind.
Sheet erosion takes place on flat agricultural lands after rainfall, removing topsoil uniformly without forming distinct channels.
Gully erosion cuts deep channels into steep, unprotected slopes, rendering the land unfit for cultivation and creating badland topography.
Human triggers such as deforestation, overgrazing, shifting cultivation, and improper farming techniques drastically accelerate erosion.
Effective conservation measures include contour plowing, terrace farming, shelterbelts, and strip cropping to bind soil and reduce runoff velocity.

rows: Uniform removal of thin topsoil layers
Cutting of deep channels and ravines into the land
Complete loss of arable land surface

items: Sheet erosion is frequently referred to as the 'silent killer' because topsoil loss occurs unnoticed over large agricultural areas.
The Chambal basin in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan is the classic Indian example of severe gully erosion resulting in badland topography.
Wind erosion dominates arid and semi-arid regions such as Western Rajasthan, where shelterbelts are used as the main defense.
